citations.authority: Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(a)(1)
citations.cited_for: Initial disclosure obligations due in the MDL
citations.context: This deadline applies to both parties' initial disclosure obligations under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(a)(1).

first_check.explanation: Rule 26(a)(1) is the initial-disclosure provision. It requires each party to provide initial disclosures without awaiting a discovery request, and it permits the timing to be set by stipulation or court order, so a court-set MDL deadline that applies to both sides is consistent with it. An MDL products-liability action is not among the exempt categories in 26(a)(1)(B). The April 15, 2025 date is a fictional scheduling fact.
first_check.evidence_excerpt: "Except as exempted by Rule 26(a)(1)(B) or as otherwise stipulated or ordered by the court, a party must, without awaiting a discovery request, provide to the other parties:" ... "at or within 14 days after the parties' Rule 26(f) conference unless a different time is set by stipulation or court order"
